summary.text:
The paper is a bookkeeping pack for Royal Wootton Bassett Town Council's Revenue & Resources Committee on 26 March 2026: a Sage-style trial balance for month 11 (April 2025 – February 2026), an earmarked reserves schedule, and a detailed balance sheet at 28/02/2026. Printed 10 March 2026 by clerk user T.FROST. It is not a treasury paper — there is no CFR, no prudential indicator, no MRP policy statement, no borrowing balance, no rate, no maturity, no strategy. The only place PWLB debt appears is a single debit line, account 4060 ‘LOAN PAYMENT-MANOR HOUSE’ at £81,331.34, servicing a Manor House loan that the paper does not otherwise scope. This is a parish-tier council reporting on a simplified basis (per the JPAG Practitioners' Guide) so the loan liability sits in the AGAR annual return rather than on this in-year balance sheet.

Our file does hold a PWLB loan for the borrower name ROYAL WOOTTON BASSETT TC (WILTS): one loan, £1,067,550 at 5.4800% weighted, ANNUITY profile, maturing 25 April 2049 (loan ref 722715). The paper's £81,331.34 charge for 11 months annualises to about £88,725, which is broadly consistent with servicing a ~£1m annuity at 5.48% with roughly 23 years to run — but ‘broadly consistent with’ is not a reconciliation. Because the paper prints no loan balance, no rate and no maturity, no loan-book claim can be quoted back to them; this is a case where the paper is silent, not one where our file and theirs disagree.

The balance-sheet identity CFR − external borrowing − OLTL = internal borrowing cannot be tested because it does not apply as printed. CFR is a Prudential Code concept that town councils do not report on this pack; external borrowing is not shown; OLTL is not shown. Recorded so the absence is not misread as an error.

What the balance sheet does show is a striking cash position. Total cash and equivalents are £1,191,999 across twelve accounts at 28/02/2026, of which £706,292 (59%) sits in the CCLA Public Sector Deposit Fund. External PWLB debt in our file is £1,067,550. Cash exceeds PWLB debt by £124,449 — a net-investor position at town-council scale. Earmarked reserves total £398,451 (closing), of which £221,567 is Manor House-related (Contingency £50k, Retention £12k, Fixtures & Fit £159,567), with a new £70k Merchant House Repair reserve created in-year and £51,765 held as CIL 2024/25. Our indicative break-cost engine puts the single 2049 annuity at a net premium of £28,186 (2.7% of principal) on the DMO curve at notice 314/26 PM — indicative only.

No email drafted. Three reasons, in order of weight. First, this is a parish-tier council, and the whole PWLBtoday outreach pipeline is built for principal authority S151 officers — the template's bridge paragraph, its standing inclusions (liability benchmark, CIPFA Prudential/Treasury Code) and its comparison set (77 principal authorities read) do not fit the audience. Second, the paper carries no treasury content in the sense the pipeline reads for; a cold email built on our net-investor observation would be inferred from figures the paper does not itself discuss, and would read as advice from a firm the council has not asked. Third, no officer address is published anywhere on the document. The observations above are recorded here for monitor state, not because they belong in a first-contact email.

contacts.note: No officer name and no email address are printed anywhere in this document. The pack is generated output (Sage trial balance + EMR schedule + balance sheet), not a member-facing committee report with a cover sheet. The trial balance and balance sheet were printed by user 'T.FROST' — clerk-side initials only, not a published contact address. Town Clerk / RFO addresses will be on the council website but are not in this pack.
